title: paged kv cache: block allocator reuse + pinning optimizations
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: The paged KV cache's block allocator has been a source of allocation churn and premature evictions under high-concurrency serving workloads. This PR improves allocator reuse, refines pinning semantics for in-flight KV blocks, and tightens TTL-based eviction to reduce costly re-loads.

Summary of changes: implement a fast reusable block freelist with epoch-based reclamation; add per-block pin counters and 'pin windows' to prevent eviction of blocks that will be immediately reaccessed; introduce a small LRU segmentation to prioritize recently-used pinned blocks; adjust TTL semantics to avoid aggressive eviction of warm prefixes; expose new runtime metrics (kv.block.reuse_hits, kv.block.pin_evictions, kv.block.reclaimed_count) and tracing spans for allocator operations.

Impact: Microbenchmarks and canary runs show 8-15% throughput improvement for bursty chat workloads and up to 20% reduction in upstream model load events. P95 latency improved by 5-12% under sustained concurrent traffic. Changes are backwards-compatible at the API level; behavior changes are internal to the cache.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests for allocator correctness and pin counter behavior added. Integration perf canary run against perf-canary (redwood/perf-canary) for 48h across a mix of request sizes and sequence lengths. Feature gated behind runtime flag (kv.paged.enable_reuse_pin) with default enabled in canary and staged rollouts.

Notes: This PR focuses on allocator/pinning logic and avoids touching kernel execution paths or batching heuristics. Follow-ups will evaluate tighter integration with continuous batching scheduler to further reduce latency tail when pinned blocks are present.

release_notes: Paged KV cache: reduce allocation churn via reusable block freelist; improves throughput for bursty workloads.
Add pinning protections to avoid evicting in-flight or immediately-reused KV blocks.
Expose kv.block.* metrics and tracing for allocator operations.
Feature gated behind kv.paged.enable_reuse_pin; default enabled in canary and staged rollouts.
benchmark_results: 8-15% throughput improvement on chat-like burst workloads (measured in perf-canary against 8x A100 mix)
5-12% p95 latency reduction under sustained concurrent traffic
Up to 20% fewer upstream model load events observed during 48h canary
notes: Follow-up: evaluate tighter integration with continuous batching scheduler to prioritize requests that benefit from pinned blocks.
Follow-up: consider exposing per-tenant pin budgets to avoid noisy-neighbor effects in multi-tenant Dedicated clusters.
